A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same homotopy-dynamics work and contain readable main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices. Retained content can be matched despite the changed title, expanded experiments and relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original Allen–Cahn, high-frequency function approximation and Burgers/DeepONet experiments, including numerical errors, losses and solution plots in Tables 1–3 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds Helmholtz experiments, additional comparator results, initialization diagnostics and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The two training strategies and loss components remain. However, Equation (9) and Algorithm 1 change the definition of Δεk from εk−1−εk to εk−εk−1, correcting the signed Euler update and finite-difference homotopy term as written. This is a localized algorithmic correction; implementation changes are not established.

E1.justification: v3 adds a 20-dimensional Helmholtz PDE experiment with increasingly oscillatory solutions, substantially extending the previous low-dimensional PDE and function-approximation coverage. All earlier tasks remain: the high-frequency function experiment moves from Section 5.2 to Appendix B.5.

E2.justification: For 2D Allen–Cahn, v3 Table 3 adds Curriculum, Time Sequential and Resampling comparators alongside the retained original PINN comparison. Appendix B.6/Table 8 additionally evaluates finite differences against homotopy-trained DeepONet for Burgers; v1 did not report this comparison.

E3.justification: Added evaluations introduce substantial protocols: 10,000 residual and 2,000 boundary points for Helmholtz; matching network architectures and specified schedules for the new Allen–Cahn comparators; 5,000 additional interface samples for resampling; and viscosity-dependent finite-difference time steps and timing comparisons. These are added protocols, not evidence that the retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Table 2 tests how Xavier versus homotopy initializations affect the minimum kernel eigenvalue at fixed target ε=0.01. Figures 13 and 15 extend the parameter-dependent spectral diagnostics to Helmholtz and Burgers. Together these substantially expand the mechanism and sensitivity evidence beyond v1's Allen–Cahn diagnostic.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new initialization comparison supplies individual eigenvalue entries without adding repeated-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The original Table 1, high-frequency results (v1 Table 2/v3 Table 7) and Burgers results (v1 Table 3/v3 Table 5) retain their values. Substantial results are added: v3 Table 4 reports Helmholtz L2RE of 9.98e-1 for classical training versus 5.89e-4 for homotopy at ε=1/50; other additions include comparator errors, initialization eigenvalues and FDM accuracy/timing. These are newly reported results, not demonstrated v1-to-v3 performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 replaces the ReLU-specific argument with analytic, nonpolynomial activation assumptions, adds nonparallel-input conditions and substantially revises the finite-width concentration proof. Theorem 4.3 now requires εn>0 rather than allowing zero. The lower spectral bound newly displayed in Theorem 4.1 already appeared in v1's proof and is not itself new theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion broaden the central claimed scope from sharp-interface problems to singularly perturbed PDEs, explicitly including high-dimensional oscillatory Helmholtz problems. The introduction also adds a claimed theoretical distinction from curriculum PINNs through continuous path tracking, convergence guarantees and principled step-size selection.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive explanations of pseudoinverse instability, the stabilizing role of homotopy-loss optimization and the need to retain PDE/boundary losses. It qualifies favorable large-ε training conditions and discusses growing Lipschitz constants near ε=0. Appendix B.6 adds interpretations of FDM cost and resolution limitations and DeepONet's suitability for repeated queries.

D1.justification: Table 6 newly discloses per-epoch times and total epochs for four examples. Appendix B adds concrete Helmholtz settings, comparator implementation controls, resampling counts and FDM time steps. Existing software, hardware and default optimizer information remain. The epoch counts are newly documented budgets, not established increases over v1.

R1.justification: v3 substantially develops its relationship to curriculum PINN regularization, previously cited without this direct novelty discussion. It expands operator-learning, multiscale-network and smooth-activation theory references, including Du et al. and Lanthaler et al. It also replaces the convergence-proof attribution to Antonakopoulos et al. with Atkinson et al.'s numerical ODE text.

P1.justification: The revision substantially reframes the narrative around singular perturbations, rewrites introductory and problem-setting passages, expands explanations of both training strategies and theory, and revises the conclusion. Moving the high-frequency experiment into Appendix B.5 also changes the main experimental narrative, although the overall section sequence remains.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redesigned to include the algorithmic phases, and Figure 5 revises its intermediate homotopy snapshots. New comparator solution panels, spectral plots and comparison/cost tables substantially expand the displays. The high-frequency figure and table are relocated to the appendix, while retained figures and tables are renumbered.

improvement.justification: The added curriculum, sequential-training and resampling comparisons address v1's limited baseline evidence; initialization diagnostics and training-cost disclosures further improve scrutiny. However, v3's stated sigmoid/softplus examples violate its new activation bound at zero (Appendix A.1), and its 20-dimensional Helmholtz experiment lists a two-input network (Appendix B.4). These inconsistencies constrain confidence in the expanded theory and coverage, limiting the overall quality gain.
